v1.1.3 — a validator with relay off gets back to the tip and votes again

No reset, no coordinated update: replace the binary and restart; data, key and stake stay. This
release changes nothing a block contains or how it is executed.

**Update before you unjail if your validator runs with `HELIX_P2P_RELAY=off`**

From 1.0.1 to 1.1.2 a validator with relay off did not hear the finished blocks its peers publish,
to save its download, and followed them by block sync instead. That fails exactly when it
matters. A validator that falls one block behind — after an unjail it starts behind by design,
because a node outside the set follows the chain at a distance — finalizes nothing itself any more:
the votes it hears are all for later heights. Every block then has to come by block sync, which
under load took 10 to 30 seconds per answer while the chain adds a block every 2.2 seconds, so it
never got back to the tip and never voted. Since protocol 2 that ends in a downtime jail with a
penalty: on 2026-10-24 the production validator was jailed again 700 blocks after it returned to
the set, and seven other validators promoted in the same epoch were jailed within the same minutes.

- **Every validator hears finished blocks again, relay on or off.** One block behind, the block the
  chain just finalized is what brings a validator back in time to vote on the next one. Relay off
  keeps its meaning: the node passes on nothing it did not write itself. Since only a block's
  proposer publishes it, this costs one copy per block from each peer that forwards it.

If your validator was jailed and runs with relay off: update to 1.1.3 first, then unjail. Running
1.1.2 or older, the next jail is likely, and under protocol 2 each one within 30 days costs more
(1 %, 3 %, then 5 % of your stake, and of your own stake that is unbonding).
